hero.subtitle: Where aesthetics is not the goal, but the natural result of a competent technical process.

projects.title: Cosmos. Moscow
projects.description: A 3D Unreal Engine scene built for the City of Moscow's cultural programme — specifically the Cosmos pavilion in one of the city parks. The piece plays on the pavilion's LED ceiling: visitors tilt their heads back and watch space drift overhead in a continuous, calm loop.
projects.assignment: Create a meditative, looping video canvas on a cosmos theme for an overhead LED ceiling. The challenge: contrasty enough to make a passer-by stop and look up, yet soft enough to hold attention for minutes without feeling monotonous or noisy.
projects.solution: Built entirely inside Unreal Engine, uniting scene assembly, shading, lighting and animation in a single real-time pipeline. Camera and procedural motion are tuned so the loop point stays hidden and the piece can run endlessly with no visible repetition.
projects.context: The result is a hypnotic, seamless ambient piece that pulls foot traffic and increases dwell time on location. Thanks to the UE build, the scene is ready for fast customization of color, scale or branding integration.

projects.title: Parfume. Simulation
projects.description: Photoreal, 'living' visualization of a perfume bottle — procedural cloth and soft-body simulation, premium lighting, and a series of seamless loops.
projects.assignment: Bring a static perfume bottle to life as a photoreal, 'living' material using 3D alone — no shoot, no physical props. The visuals had to work in premium product retail and in social feeds, with cinematic environmental motion that emphasizes the product's form and character.
projects.solution: Production spans three systems: complex procedural cloth and soft-body simulations in Houdini, final shading, premium lighting and render in Blender, and the final grade in DaVinci Resolve. The procedural setup instantly generates a whole series of angles and seamless loops from a single source.
projects.context: The output is a flexible visual system and a series of seamless loops with photoreal material and fabric behavior. The engineered pipeline delivers premium commercial visuals and lets the scene be re-customized for other products in the line without rebuilding from scratch.

projects.title: Hoodi
projects.description: 3D product visualization of a hoodie with full garment modeling and cloth simulation. The piece replaces a photo shoot — fabric character, folds, fit, and lighting are all built and rendered in CG.
projects.assignment: Translate a hoodie product photo into pure CG — material, folds, fit. Keep the cut recognisable and the fabric character intact at any zoom.
projects.solution: Base pattern is built in Marvelous Designer and groomed in Blender; the simulation is layered so the silhouette stays clean while micro-folds and seams stay tangible. Physically-based fabric maps drive the lookdev.
projects.context: The setup is reused as a template for product graphics for apparel brands — same scene, swap garment patterns and lookdev maps.

projects.title: ThyName. Worship Visuals
projects.description: End-to-end stage visuals for church worship services and recurring Bible marathons — a single dynamic visual system that seamlessly bridges transitions between speakers, carries the mission, and scales with ease. Event motto: 'Praising Thy Name — we find our own names.'
projects.assignment: Hold the room's attention and cut the cost of constantly refreshing content. Speaker changes created technical pauses that broke the emotional rhythm and scattered attention; events run year-round, so the visuals had to adapt by season without rebuilding the scene from scratch.
projects.solution: The concept centers on a faceless figure running through life: interacting with the space it slows, rises, and finally takes form — a direct translation of the mission, 'every runner finds their name.' The pipeline splits into four modular blocks (Prologue, Intro, Thematic inserts, Finale) that flex in length to match the live timing and seamlessly fill any pause. Animation splines and the character stay fixed; atmosphere and season change only through light, particle systems and procedural environment — updates at minimal cost.
projects.context: Visual and technical pauses between speakers were fully removed; the graphics hold attention through scene changes and became part of the overall narrative. The result is a scalable base that adapts content to any season or format quickly and with minimal render.

projects.title: MetallPlace
projects.description: Two motion pieces for the metallplace.ru information portal — a tight brand loop for digital touchpoints and a long-form lecture cut for internal education. One visual system, two very different runtimes.
projects.assignment: Translate the portal's brand kit into two formats: a short loop that lives on social and partner LED screens, and a lecture cut that explains the product to suppliers and buyers at MetallConf and internal sessions.
projects.solution: Both pieces share the same 2D toolkit in After Effects — palette, typographic system, motion curves. The brand loop runs tight and rhythmic; the lecture cut breathes, leaves room for voiceover, and threads through the portal's product features end-to-end.
projects.context: Used in the portal's public channels, in MetallConf 2023 keynote decks, and in internal product onboarding for new suppliers and buyers.

projects.title: Batara Travel
projects.description: 2D motion design for a travel agency — frame-by-frame brand storytelling assembled in After Effects.
projects.assignment: Translate the agency's identity into a short looping spot that reads on social feeds and on partner LED screens.
projects.solution: Layout, animation and final grade live in After Effects. The cut keeps a calm rhythm so the type and the destinations remain the lead actors.
projects.context: Used by the agency in social channels and inside their offline presentations.

faq.title: Questions Clients Ask
faq.subtitle: Straight answers on cost, timelines, the process and how we'd work together — for brands, founders and studios.

items.q: How much does a 3D product visualization or animation cost?
items.a: Every project is priced individually — it depends on the complexity, detail and length. Entry-level projects like a product render or short animation start from 18,000 ₽ or $250. Message me with your task and I'll send an accurate estimate and timeline within the day.

items.q: How long does a 3D visualization or animation take?
items.a: A single product render usually takes a few days, a short animated spot about 2–4 weeks, larger campaigns longer. After a short brief I give you a firm timeline with clear milestones. For a launch, booking 4–8 weeks ahead is comfortable.

items.q: Why choose 3D instead of a photo or video shoot?
items.a: With 3D you're not limited by the physical product, a location or shooting logistics — it can be shown from any angle, color or environment and reused across ads, web and social without reshooting. Ideal when the product doesn't exist yet or needs many variations.

items.q: Can you create a 3D animation or ad for a new product launch?
items.a: Yes — it's one of my core services. We align on goal, audience, budget and deadline, then I show a moodboard and references for your sign-off before any animation starts. You approve the look early and receive a final video cut for every platform (Instagram, YouTube, your site).

items.q: Do you work with studios and agencies as a freelance CG generalist or Houdini FX artist?
items.a: Yes. I join studio and agency teams as extra experienced hands — lighting, rendering and especially the complex effects and simulations (cloth, liquids, smoke, particles) that need a dedicated specialist. I work in your team's formats (After Effects, DaVinci Resolve) and hand off clean project files.

items.q: What do you need from me to start a project?
items.a: Just a short description of your goal, any references or brand materials, your deadline and a rough budget. From there I scope the work, give you a clear timeline and price, and we agree on review rounds. No technical or 3D knowledge needed on your side.

items.q: What kinds of projects do you take on?
items.a: Product visualization, animated commercials and explainers, effect-driven and procedural animation (cloth, liquids, smoke, particles), motion design, and pipeline or automation help for studios. Not sure your project fits? Message me and I'll tell you honestly.

items.q: Why use CG instead of AI generators?
items.a: AI generators are great for quick ideas, but they can't reliably reproduce your exact product, logo or materials, they drift between frames, and rarely give clean, editable output you own. CG gives full control — accurate from every angle, art-directable, with physically correct simulations.

items.q: Do you combine AI with CG?
items.a: Yes — that's where the best results come from. I use AI to speed up ideation, references and texture exploration, then build the final, brand-accurate and fully controllable result in CG. You get the speed of AI with the precision and consistency of real production.
